title: Integration by file, by database, by API and by event

videos.script: Serra Alta has a hundred and ten integrations. Joana counted them by hand, over five weeks. {{map}} For thirty-eight of them, nobody could say how a failure would be noticed. That is the question this lesson teaches you to ask. {{unknown}} Every integration moves data in one of four ways. By file, written now and read later. By sharing a database. By calling an API and waiting for the answer. Or by publishing an event that anybody may receive. {{styles}} Each style ties the two systems together differently. In the format they agree on. In whether both must be up at once. In whether one knows where the other is. And each one fails in its own way. A file that never arrives. A table that quietly changes meaning. A call that times out with a customer waiting. A lag that grows with no error at all. {{failures}} You will read a short program that writes a farm collection file safely, and refuses a copy with one line missing. {{program}} Then Joana takes six real integrations and decides each one. Some change style. Most keep the one they have, with an alarm they never had. {{decisions}}
